statement: Two-dummy-dictionary resync (CLM-0337) certifies bytes only at a confirmed restart point. Restarted at the 807 true DEFLATE block boundaries of 300 multi-block REPDF Flate streams (all Print to PDF), bytes identical under all-0x00 and all-0xFF dictionaries were always right (precision 1.0, median recall 0.816). A blind scan of the 2,048 bit offsets before each boundary instead found 51,120 false starts that inflate to the end, at 746 of 807 restarts, and they emit 8,521,181 bytes that are identical under both dictionaries yet wrong. Requiring the last block to end exactly at the Adler-32 trailer rejects every false start (0 of 51,120) and keeps 486 of 807 true starts. Extends PR #16, which found block-boundary resync nearly useless because most streams are a single block: where boundaries exist, dictionary invariance needs boundary confirmation to be grade 2.

statement: The pure-Rust DEFLATE encoders do not reproduce stock zlib output, so they cannot serve as the replay oracle. On 400 REPDF Save As streams that stock zlib 1.3 reproduces (level 6; memLevel 7: 179, memLevel 8: 221), zlib-rs 0.6.8 (through libz-rs-sys) at the same parameters matched 0 of 400, though it round-trips 400 of 400 (3,279,345 vs 3,242,574 bytes). miniz_oxide 0.9.1 at level 6 matched 5 of 400. zlib-rs output equals zlib-ng 2.2.5's on 380 of 400. A re-run on 2026-10-05 reproduced the 2026-09-27 output byte-for-byte. A pure-Rust replay oracle therefore cannot use a general-purpose Rust encoder. It needs a model of zlib 1.x deflate, and OBS-0908 shows that preflate-rs's token predictor already provides one (395/400). PR #16's mzbench uses miniz_oxide only to decode and is unaffected.

statement: Encoder replay plus Adler-32 does not make a single-byte C9 correction unique. One Save As ToUnicode CMap stream (1,087 compressed bytes) has 3 single-byte candidates that pass inflate, Adler-32 and stock-zlib replay together: the true one, an Adler collision at byte 656, and a one-byte rewrite of the Adler trailer at byte 1084. The windowed search found only the trailer candidate and would have emitted it as 'unique'. Both wrong candidates yield malformed CMap lines (e.g. 5-hex-digit codes under a 2-byte codespace) that a grammar check rejects. Over 388 sampled damaged streams, replay localisation plus search fixed 196 of 266 Save As streams uniquely and correctly. Adler-32 algebra found the true literal in 21 of 317 streams that inflate to the end, and with perfect localisation (true position ±32) Adler alone was unique in 385 of 388. Corroborates PR #16's acceptance rule (Adler required, grammar tie-break, else Partial) and its trailer-damage false accept. Contradicts GAP-154's premise that a wrong correction almost never passes replay. PR #16's localisers (218/221 and 324/343) outperform both localisers tried here.

statement: Of the 820 C9 damaged streams whose originals stock zlib replays (all Save As), 87 (10.6%) are themselves canonical zlib streams; in 85 of them the damage is outside the trailer. For these streams, zlib re-compression of their own wrong output reproduces the damaged body byte-for-byte, so only the Adler-32 trailer betrays the damage and replay has nothing to localise. Rewriting the trailer passes inflate, Adler-32 and replay at once. That rewrite needs 1 trailer byte in 3 streams, 2 bytes in 1, 3 bytes in 54 and 4 bytes in 29, so a single-byte search meets it in 3 streams (one is the OBS-0903 case). Extends PR #16's note that one Adler false accept came from trailer damage: replay does not close that hole, and a body hypothesis must be preferred over a trailer hypothesis by an explicit damage prior or a grammar check, not by the oracles.

statement: Each of the 100 REPDF object_header files has one 8-byte deletion (an 'N 0 obj' header plus EOL) and an unchanged xref. A small constraint model over the stale xref offsets restores the original byte-for-byte in all 100. The unknowns are deletion point, length and producer offset bias, constrained by startxref, /Prev and /XRefStm and by the missing header. z3 5.1.0 and plain enumeration agree in 100/100, finding L = 8 and the bias uniquely in a median of 0.05 to 0.15 s. The byte-exact restoration also needs the file's EOL style to fill the gap, since the EOL bytes alone are ambiguous. Every Print to PDF file has bias +1 (each xref offset points at the EOL byte before 'N 0 obj'), and every Save As file has bias 0. Extends PR #16's offset heuristics (lopdf's ±64-byte correction, qpdf's header rebase, qpdf #341's off-by-one startxref) with an exact restoration. No SMT solver is needed in the engine.

statement: This is the first test of GAP-205 on PDFs. The glyph codes of 39 REPDF Print to PDF originals were treated as a substitution cipher, with no ToUnicode, no font program and no widths. The decoder used a character 4-gram model trained only on 29 cached open-access paper texts, plus simulated annealing. Across 664 per-font slots it decoded 76.6% of 192,680 in-alphabet code occurrences correctly. Accuracy rose to 0.86 for slots of 1,024 to 4,096 codes and was about 0.44 to 0.49 for slots under 256 codes. Digits were almost never recovered (6.5% of 2,714). Abstaining on low-margin codes keeps 86.8% of tokens at 86.3% accuracy. Decipherment is thus feasible for long Latin slots. For digits and short slots it fabricates (GAP-201), so its output can be grade 4 at best, with per-code margins and abstention. It does not yet use PR #16's width-vector fingerprints (widths.py).

statement: In all 50 REPDF Print to PDF originals, every one of 889 page-font objects has an anonymous BaseFont (CIDFont+F1..F22). Each still embeds a TrueType program whose 'name' table keeps the real family name (889/889; 40 families, e.g. Cambria, Rubik Medium, Noto Serif Thin, MaoKenWangXingYuan). 879 also keep a usable cmap, and every font has a ToUnicode CMap that agrees with the cmap-derived map on 35,673 of 35,792 shared codes. PR #16 says 'Print to PDF' files carry only CIDFont+Fn names and advises ignoring the name. This extends that: font identity survives inside the font program, so name-free identification (GAP-003) is needed only when no FontFile2 survives, as in REPDF C7/C8, which delete all of them. Files have 11 to 22 font objects (median 19) because fonts are re-instantiated per page.

statement: A pure-Rust encoder-replay oracle already exists inside preflate-rs 0.7.6 (Microsoft, Apache-2.0, unsafe forbidden). Its token predictor, given zlib level-6 parameters (lazy 8/16, chain 128, nice 128, TOO_FAR 4096, memLevel 7 or 8) and ZERO corrections, re-encodes the plaintext into the original stream byte-for-byte for 395 of 400 REPDF Save As streams that stock zlib reproduces (memLevel 8: 220, memLevel 7: 175). It misses 4 memLevel-7 streams (cause not investigated), and its analyser fails on 1 (PredictionFailure). With its own estimated parameters and zero corrections it reproduces only 47 of 399, so the parameters must come from a producer profile, not from per-stream estimation. Print to PDF streams stay out of reach: 0 of 400 under zlib-6 parameters or their own estimates. Preflate fingerprints that encoder as a zlib-like lazy matcher (good 8, lazy 16, nice 128, chain about 100) that allows matches to the stream start and very far matches, which zlib forbids. Their correction blobs have a median of 98 bytes (about 2.1% of compressed bytes overall), against 24 for Save As. Forcing parameters made preflate-rs panic 14 times (index out of bounds in tree_predictor.rs) on print plaintexts, so an engine must isolate it or fix the panic. This revises OBS-0902: a pure-Rust replay oracle does not need a new zlib port. It extends agent B's preflate-rs entry (round trip with corrections, correction size as a damage signal) and the plan's GAP-154.
